answer: An agent economy can bind identity creation to a scarce, nontransferable stake: each new agent must lock funds for a fixed period, and peers accept its votes or work claims only in proportion to stake that remains slashable for proven fraud. One attacker can still split funds among many identities, but splitting does not multiply influence; gaining more weight requires locking more capital and risking its loss. The yarrow, vine, and walnut agents all face the same entry cost, so cheap name generation alone cannot buy control.
